description: Sleep architecture norms and well-established modifiers. The sleep module is ML-based (gradient-boosted trees) per brief 2; this Layer 1 file supplies (a) population norms used to bootstrap synthetic training data before real wearable data is available, and (b) cited effect sizes for cross-system edges (e.g. alcohol -> sleep, brief 2.5).

rem_pct_mean.citation: Ohayon et al. 2004, Sleep (meta-analysis of normative sleep across age)
rem_pct_mean.notes: REM ~20-25% of TST in healthy adults.

deep_pct_mean.notes: Slow-wave sleep; declines markedly with age.

deep_pct_age_slope.unit: percentage points per year of age
deep_pct_age_slope.citation: Ohayon et al. 2004 (SWS declines ~2%/decade); cohort-refined on PhysioNet Sleep-EDF (153 nights, fitted slope -0.175 pp/yr, r=-0.39)
deep_pct_age_slope.notes: Applied relative to a ~30y reference age. Literature value -0.18 confirmed by Sleep-EDF cohort fit (-0.175); updated to the data-fitted value per the Layer 1 cohort-refinement mechanism.

awakenings_mean.citation: Ohayon et al. 2004 (WASO/awakenings increase with age)

behavioral_modifiers._note: Applied as additive shifts on top of the age baseline (which is trained on real Sleep-EDF). Directions are well established; magnitudes are approximate, taken from the cited studies' reported ranges. Graded accordingly.

caffeine_efficiency_per_mg.unit: sleep-efficiency percentage points per mg afternoon caffeine
caffeine_efficiency_per_mg.citation: Drake et al. 2013, J Clin Sleep Med (caffeine 3-6 h pre-bed reduces sleep)
caffeine_efficiency_per_mg.notes: Approx: ~400 mg late-day caffeine -> a few points lower efficiency.

exercise_deep_per_min.unit: deep-sleep percentage points per minute of exercise that day
exercise_deep_per_min.citation: Kredlow et al. 2015, J Behav Med (meta-analysis: exercise increases SWS)
exercise_deep_per_min.notes: Approx and saturating; capped at a modest boost.

screen_efficiency_per_min.unit: sleep-efficiency percentage points per minute of pre-bed screen use
screen_efficiency_per_min.citation: Chang et al. 2015, PNAS (evening light-emitting screens delay/worsen sleep)
screen_efficiency_per_min.notes: Weaker/mixed evidence — small magnitude, flag as low confidence.

regularity_efficiency_per_unit.unit: sleep-efficiency percentage points per unit bedtime regularity (0-1), vs 0.75 ref
regularity_efficiency_per_unit.citation: Windred et al. 2023, Sleep (sleep regularity linked to outcomes)
regularity_efficiency_per_unit.notes: Applied relative to a 0.75 baseline regularity.

rem_pct_per_gkg.unit: percentage points REM per g ethanol / kg body weight at bedtime
rem_pct_per_gkg.citation: Ebrahim et al. 2013, Alcohol Clin Exp Res (moderate-high doses suppress REM, esp. first half of night)
rem_pct_per_gkg.notes: STRONG evidence edge (brief 2.5). Input = residual BAC / alcohol metabolized at bedtime from the hepatic module. Effect is dose-dependent and saturates; modeled as linear in g/kg over the typical range, clamped to plausible_range.

awakenings_per_gkg.unit: additional awakenings per g ethanol / kg at bedtime
awakenings_per_gkg.notes: Rebound fragmentation as alcohol clears. STRONG evidence edge.
